idiom_name: Logger with a custom device/formatter chaining OpenSSL::HMAC
implementation_notes: Ruby's stdlib Logger already separates the chokepoint from the destination: give it a custom device (or subclass and override write) plus a formatter that canonicalises the message, then chain OpenSSL::HMAC.digest('SHA256', key, prev + seq + body) and append the tag; Logger's own rotation, severity and progname handling stay usable. The hand-written writer is justified when the audit stream must outlive Logger configuration churn - a dedicated writer object keeps the chain state away from the rotation path that resets devices.
pitfalls: Logger rotates through its own LogDevice when size or age limits hit; each rotation resets the device, so the head authenticator must be anchored before rotation or whole files disappear without a detectable break.
Ruby strings are mutable: tag the exact bytes you write (frozen literals or .b) instead of a String a caller can still modify between digest and write.

OpenSSL::HMAC.digest allocates per record and the chain state is not protected by the GVL across processes - fork-based servers (Puma, Unicorn workers) each inherit a copy, so pin one writer process per chain.
